interpretation.tailMetricCaveat: p95 and max represent the same observation here and are not independent adverse results.
interpretation.outcome: This same-source control records variation between isolated contexts running identical source content. It does not show that adverse original baseline/current observations are nonexistent or caused solely by noise. The original comparison remains separate and unchanged.
interpretation.scope: Trusted click/change capture to the second requestAnimationFrame callback at 1920x1080, low effects, SwiftShader. This is not render/paint completion, FPS, physical-device/GPU performance, or a storage benchmark.
interpretation.generalization: Twelve repeated pairs per synthetic fixture/action are descriptive observations. They do not establish statistical significance or representative real-user latency.

sourceReview: The capture listener starts before the product bubble handlers. The nested rAF endpoint is accurately named and intentionally excludes later card/save verification work.
Native Playwright click and keyboard actions are checked through event.isTrusted and final select value; the driver does not call the sorting function as the timed user input.
The 60-card requirement follows from exact full oracle-array equality for these unfiltered fixtures; every recorded row was additionally checked for explicit cardinality 60 here.
Both complete persisted strings are compared with the original schema5 fixture after every action, retaining unknown metadata. The fixture is explicitly synthetic.
Odd/even AB/BA orders, separate warmup rows, fixed deadlines, unchanged source/driver hashes, served-source verification and absence of retry loops agree with the report protocol.
No unresolved product or browser-harness correctness issue was identified in this limited source-and-existing-evidence review.
